levels.title: Energy business foundations
levels.outcome: Explain an energy company’s place in the system, its sources, technologies, assets, stakeholders and physical and commercial flows.

lessons.title: From primary energy to useful services
Map an Energy Company
topics: Where does it sit in the energy system?
What energy sources does it work with?
Which value chains does it participate in?
What are its major physical assets?
Where does its energy come from?
What infrastructure does it depend on?
What units/KPIs would you use to measure its energy activities?
What happens if one critical part of its energy system fails?
lessons.objective: Select an actual energy company. Use dated, referenced sources to answer all 15 questions and draw its complete energy-system/value-chain map.
lessons.success: A referenced company map covering physical flows, commercial flows, assets, stakeholders, measurements and a critical failure scenario.

levels.title: Energy industries & technologies
levels.outcome: Explain how the major energy sectors work and connect.

levels.title: Energy economics
levels.outcome: Explain energy decisions using costs, incentives, externalities and investment economics.

levels.title: Markets, trading & contracts
levels.outcome: Explain how energy is priced, contracted and traded.

levels.title: Energy companies & business models
levels.outcome: Explain how different energy companies create and capture value.

levels.title: Operations & asset management
levels.outcome: Assess operations, assets, reliability and performance from a business perspective.

levels.title: Energy finance & investment
levels.outcome: Evaluate an energy investment using explicit financial assumptions.

levels.title: Policy, regulation & geopolitics
levels.outcome: Identify institutional constraints and stakeholder obligations.

levels.title: Risk & resilience
levels.outcome: Build a risk register and compare resilience responses.

levels.title: Sustainability & decarbonization
levels.outcome: Assess emissions, sustainability choices and trade-offs.

levels.title: Energy transition
levels.outcome: Compare transition pathways within the wider energy system.

levels.title: Digital transformation
levels.outcome: Evaluate digital opportunities and their operational dependencies.

levels.title: Analytics & decision-making
levels.outcome: Use data and uncertainty to support a decision.

levels.title: Projects & delivery
levels.outcome: Develop a delivery plan and evidence of benefits.

levels.title: Strategy
levels.outcome: Choose where to compete and explain how to win.

levels.title: Innovation
levels.outcome: Assess, test and scale an innovation opportunity.

levels.title: Commercial development
levels.outcome: Develop a customer, partnership and commercial approach.

levels.title: Leadership & organizations
levels.outcome: Lead change with attention to people, governance and ethics.

levels.title: Global energy systems
levels.outcome: Connect developments across countries and energy markets.

levels.title: Integrated strategy & innovation
levels.outcome: Integrate the pathway into a defensible investment and innovation recommendation.

lessons.title: Design a five-year energy investment portfolio
lessons.objective: An integrated energy company has $5 billion to invest over five years. Compare the options, state assumptions, assess risks and recommend a portfolio with an innovation roadmap.
lessons.success: An evidence-backed investment recommendation, scenarios, implementation roadmap and measures of success.
